title: Top Account Arbitration Playbook: timeboxed commitments and negotiable scope lanes
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Define a defensible, timeboxed arbitration and commitment protocol for top accounts that balances predictable engineering capacity with negotiated, deliverable scope. This ticket captures the playbook, acceptance criteria, tooling changes, stakeholder training plan, and launch gating for the arbitration flow used when high-value customers request roadmap commitments or escalations.
background: Sales and Customer Success have repeatedly requested hard commitments for top accounts that conflict with sprint capacity and OKR prioritization. Current ad-hoc promises create delivery risk, broken trust, and noisy escalation threads. We need a repeatable process that preserves customer confidence while protecting engineering delivery and roadmap integrity.
goals: Create a clear arbitration flow for requests from top accounts that yields either a timeboxed commitment, a negotiated scope with SLA, or a formal deferral
Provide tooling in the roadmap intake form and Console to surface arbitration decisions and remaining scope items
Reduce unplanned sprint churn from VIP commitments by 60% within two quarters
Make negotiation outcomes auditable and traceable to avoid future disputes
success_metrics: % reduction in emergency ticket creation from top accounts (target: -60% in 2 quarters)
% of top-account requests resolved within arbitration SLA window (target: 95% within 10 business days)
Customer satisfaction for negotiated commitments (CSAT target >= 4.2/5)
Number of roadmap rollbacks caused by VIP commitments (target: 0 per quarter)
Time to publish arbitration decision to customer and internal stakeholders (target <= 48 hours after decision)
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document published in Confluence with step-by-step flow and escalation matrix
Intake form updated with arbitration flag, mandatory business impact, and desired SLA window
Automated scorecard implemented that outputs recommended lane: Committed (timeboxed), Conditional (negotiated scope + SLA), Defer
Console roadmap view includes an 'Arbitration' column and visible expiration/commitment windows
Training session completed for Sales, CS, and PMs with sign-off from VP of GTM
Two pilot arbitrations completed with real customers and documented learnings
tasks: PM: Draft arbitration playbook and decision rubric
Eng: Implement arbitration flag and scorecard in intake API and database
Design: Create Console UI for Arbitration column and commitment banners
PM Ops: Coordinate two pilot customers and prepare success metrics dashboard
Legal: Draft templated commitment language and optional SOW clauses
GTM: Prepare customer-facing comms templates for commitment outcomes
Training: Run two live walkthroughs and collect feedback
Data: Build dashboard showing request volume, resolution times, and downstream sprint impact
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-committing to customers to avoid short-term churn. Mitigation: enforce mandatory engineering acceptance step and timeboxing limits
Risk: Tooling changes add friction to intake and slow response times. Mitigation: keep arbitration form minimal and pre-populate fields from CRM
Risk: Sales-side pushback on conditional or deferred outcomes. Mitigation: create compensation playbook and escalation runway with leadership involvement
Risk: Ambiguous scope in commitments leading to disputes. Mitigation: require templated scope bullets and reference artifacts in the decision record
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: Finalize playbook, decision rubric, legal templates
Week 3-4: Implement intake changes and Console UI mockups; run internal alpha
Week 5-6: Pilot with two top accounts, collect metrics and customer feedback
Week 7: Revise playbook from pilots and prepare public GTM comms
Week 8: Full launch to Sales, CS, and PM teams with training and dashboards
notes: Avoid creating a special-case fast-pass lane that bypasses engineering triage. The goal is negotiated clarity, not preferential backlog insertion. Pilot customers should have strong exec sponsorship and well-defined success metrics. We'll iterate the rubric after the first two pilots to validate thresholds.
decisions: Decision: Arbitration window default = 10 business days; can be shortened by mutual consent
Decision: Three outcome lanes: Committed (timeboxed + prioritized), Conditional (scope negotiated + SLA), Defer
Decision: Engineering acceptance required before 'Committed' label is applied
Decision: All commitments get an expiration date and a Program Manager review prior to launch
follow_up: Re-evaluate rubric thresholds after 6 pilot cases
Add a periodic audit to measure drift between committed scope and delivered scope
Consider adding a lightweight 'commitment insurance' budget in roadmap planning for Q3
